reports.title: Report on the Annual Update of the Remuneration and Pensions of Officials and Other Servants of the European Union
reports.description: Eurostat's statutory annual report under Annex XI, Article 1(1) to the Staff Regulations, which drives the mechanical calculation (Joint Index × Specific Indicator) behind the annual update of EU staff pay and pensions. Named in full at footnote 3 of COM(2025) 736: 'Eurostat Report of 31 October 2025 on the 2025 annual update of remuneration and pensions of EU officials in accordance with Articles 64 and 65 and Annexes XI to the Staff Regulations...' (C736-03). Eurostat's own publications page lists one linked report per year from 2004 to 2025 under file titles of the pattern 'Eurostat Remuneration Report [year]' (ERR-02).
reports.cadence_note: Eurostat's own Publications page: 'Reports are typically released in late October, with reference date July' (ERR-01), confirmed by 22 consecutive years of linked reports (2004-2025). Matches Annex XI Article 1(1): Eurostat 'shall draw up every year before the end of October a report' (AXI-01).

entries.covers: 2026 annual update of remuneration and pensions (reference date July 2026)

release_schedule.rule: Annex XI, Article 1(1) to the Staff Regulations: Eurostat 'shall draw up every year before the end of October a report on the adjustment of remuneration...' (AXI-01). Confirmed by publisher practice: the 2025 edition PDF (Ares(2025)9371644) was published to Eurostat's site on 2025-10-31, consistent with the corpus's cadence_note of '22 consecutive years of linked reports (2004-2025)' released in late October with reference date July.
release_schedule.note: This confirms the existing cadence_note rather than correcting it. Verified the 2025 report (Ares(2025)9371644, filename 'Eurostat Remuneration Report 2025') was published/timestamped 2025-10-31 on ec.europa.eu, matching the stated pattern of late-October release. Next edition (2026, reference date July 2026) is expected before end of October 2026 per Annex XI Article 1(1).

dependencies.basis: Annex XI to the Staff Regulations, Article 1(2) (AXI-02, EU/AnnexXI-StaffRegulations_PartA_2026-08-05.md): 'Eurostat shall draw up an index to measure changes in the cost of living for officials of the Union in Belgium and Luxembourg. That index (hereinafter the "Joint Index") shall be calculated by weighting national inflation (as measured by the Harmonised Indices of Consumer Prices (HICP) in the case of Belgium and the Consumer Prices Index (CPI) in the case of Luxembourg) between June of the previous year and June of the current year according to the distribution of the staff serving in those Member States.' The Joint Index is itself an attribute of this report, not a separate publication (AXI-05 NOTES), and Article 3(2) states the update 'shall be obtained by multiplying the Joint Index by the specific indicator' (AXI-05) -- so HICP's figures reach the report's own arithmetic through the Joint Index. Resolves the no-node-yet lead recorded in eurostat-hicp.json's _dropped block.

Annex XI, Article 1(4) (AXI-04, EU/AnnexXI-StaffRegulations_PartA_2026-08-05.md): 'The results per country shall be weighted in proportion to the appropriate national GDP aggregate measured using purchasing power parities as shown in the most recent statistics published in accordance with the national accounts definitions in the European System of Accounts currently in force... One such indicator shall be in the form of data on real per capita emoluments in central government, drawn up in accordance with the national accounts definitions in the European System of Accounts currently in force.' methodology_depends_on rather than uses_data_from, matching the esa-2010 precedent already in the corpus (de-destatis-national-accounts.json): ESA 2010 supplies accounting definitions and classifications, not figures.

RESOLVED AND VERIFIED DIRECTLY BY THIS SESSION (2026-08-09). The identification is documented after all -- by definitional property rather than by acronym, which is why three prior searches for the string 'IPCN' missed it. Eurostat's own methodological annex to the Joint Index, 'Remuneration and Pensions Calculation of the Joint Index in accordance with Annex XI of the EU Staff Regulations' (ec.europa.eu/eurostat/cache/metadata/Annexes/prc_colc_tot_esms_an_2.pdf, fetched in full this session), names the Luxembourg component as "the Consumer Prices Index (CPI) in the case of Luxembourg", sourced from "the Luxembourg national statistical office (Statec)", and then defines it: "The current Luxembourg national index of consumer prices came into effect in 1997. It complies with the HICP except that its weighting structure excludes the consumer spending of non-residents on Luxembourg territory." STATEC's own methodology document 'L'indice des prix a la consommation (IPC)' (statistiques.public.lu, /fr/methodologie/methodes/economie-finances/Prix/ipc/IPC-description.pdf, fetched in full this session) gives that exclusion as the SOLE difference between its two indices, and assigns it to the IPCN: "l'IPCN exclut les depenses de consommation finale effectuees par des non-residents sur le territoire economique luxembourgeois alors que l'IPCH les inclut", and "L'IPCN et l'IPCH sont etablis selon les memes principes methodologiques. Les deux indices se distinguent sur le seul point de leur couverture geographique." Since the two indices differ on exactly one property, and Eurostat states that property, the identification is unique: the Joint Index's Luxembourg CPI is the IPCN, not the IPCH. STATED LIMIT, per sec.3: no document read writes 'IPCN' and 'the Consumer Prices Index (CPI) in the case of Luxembourg' in the same sentence. This is an identification by matching definitions across two primary sources, not a citation. Recorded as such rather than as a quoted equivalence. MINOR DATE TENSION, logged not resolved: Eurostat dates the current national index to 1997, while STATEC writes that "le Luxembourg a decide, en janvier 2000, de reintroduire l'indice national pour les besoins de l'<<echelle mobile des salaires>>" -- consistent if the index existed from 1997 and was adopted for wage indexation in 2000, but neither document says so.

_dropped.why: RESOLVED 2026-08-09 (cheap-check pass) -- MINTED as `eurostat-remuneration-update-report -> lu-statec-ipcn` (`uses_data_from`); see that edge's `basis` for the full quotes. The answer is IPCN. WHY THREE PRIOR SEARCHES MISSED IT, which is the transferable lesson: the identification is stated as a DEFINITION, never as an acronym. Eurostat's Joint Index methodological annex defines the Luxembourg component as the national index whose "weighting structure excludes the consumer spending of non-residents on Luxembourg territory", and STATEC's own methodology document gives that exclusion as the single property separating IPCN from IPCH. Searching for the string 'IPCN' in EU-side documents was never going to find it; matching definitions across the two sides was. CORRECTION to this entry's own same-day UPDATE (ERR-09), which read Eurostat's Methodology page phrase 'the Luxembourg CPI (domestic concept)' as "consistent with STATEC's own description of the IPCN's resident-population-only coverage". That inference should NOT be relied on, independently of the conclusion happening to be right: in standard ESS terminology the domestic concept is the territory-based one -- it INCLUDES non-residents' spending on the territory -- while the national concept is the resident-based one. Read that way, 'domestic concept' points at the IPCH, the opposite of what the update concluded, and the Belgian label 'national concept' sits equally oddly on an HICP. The parenthetical labels on that page are not a safe basis for either reading and the edge deliberately does not rest on them. ORIGINAL ENTRY BELOW. Annex XI Article 1(2) names 'the Consumer Prices Index (CPI) in the case of Luxembourg' as the Luxembourg-side component of the Joint Index, alongside Belgium's HICP. Whether this 'CPI' identifies lu-statec-ipcn (Luxembourg's national CPI) or lu-statec-ipch (Luxembourg's harmonised CPI) -- both minted this session, EU/STATEC-CPI_PartA_2026-08-05.md -- is not stated in any document read in this branch. STATEC's own regulation's parallel HICP/CPI split (STATEC-01) reads as consistent with 'CPI' meaning the IPCN specifically, but that is a reading, not a documented identification. Searched: Annex XI's own text, COM(2025) 736, and Luxembourg's Règlement grand-ducal du 20 décembre 1999 -- none names the equivalence. UPDATE, same-day continuation session (ERR-09, EU/EurostatRemunerationReport_PartA_2026-08-05.md): Eurostat's own Methodology page describes the Joint Index calculation's starting point as 'the Belgium HICP (national concept) and the Luxembourg CPI (domestic concept)' -- 'domestic concept' reads as consistent with STATEC's own description of the IPCN's resident-population-only coverage. Corroborating, still not a documented identification -- no document anywhere in this branch writes 'IPCN' and 'domestic concept' as the same thing. Reason stays no-document.
